local.h: USDA presses on with Forest Service overhaul
local.b: Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins says the administration is 'full-bore ahead' on reorganizing the Forest Service after a judge blocked it. Georgia's office in Athens would stay open under the plan.
local.title: Ag secretary: Agency is 'full-bore ahead' on Forest Service overhaul

local.h: Fields Corner Post Office will stay open
local.b: In a last-minute reversal, USPS secured a lease extension for the Fields Corner Post Office in Dorchester, which was set to close Monday.
local.title: In last-minute reversal, Fields Corner Post Office will stay open

local.h: Hasbro CEO explains move to Boston
local.b: Hasbro CEO Chris Cocks spoke with WBUR about relocating the toymaker to Boston's Seaport after more than 100 years in Rhode Island.
local.title: Hasbro's CEO on the company's relocation to Boston

local.h: Harvard Book Store opening downtown Boston shop
local.b: Harvard Book Store plans to open a second location at 33 Union St. in downtown Boston this fall. The Cambridge store will remain the flagship.

local.h: DOJ joins suit against Evanston reparations
local.b: A federal judge let the Justice Department join a Judicial Watch class-action challenge to Evanston's reparations program for Black residents, which launched in 2021.
local.title: DOJ allowed to join lawsuit against Evanston reparations program for Black residents

local.h: Salt Shed owners eye amphitheater expansion
local.b: A zoning application seeks to expand Salt Shed's entertainment holdings onto a plot at 1401-59 N. Magnolia Ave. across from the West Town venue.
local.title: Salt Shed owners eye amphitheater expansion across from popular West Town venue

local.h: Kennedy Expressway delays persist
local.b: A WBEZ and Sun-Times analysis of 22 years of drive-time data finds Kennedy Expressway delays persist a year after the three-year construction project ended.
local.title: 3 years after Kennedy Expressway rehab, traffic is still a nightmare

local.h: CPS approves $300K for family of bullied girl
local.b: The school board approved a settlement for the mother of a Black student who endured more than two years of racist bullying at a Northwest Side school.

local.h: CPS lunchroom workers win raises, avert strike
local.b: The board approved a new contract for about 1,500 lunchroom workers that raises wage floors after more than a year of talks.

goodnews.b: A UChicago Consortium report finds CPS students are graduating and enrolling in college at higher rates and earning more college credits in high school, though many still struggle to finish degrees.

local.h: Metrolink halts Oceanside service for high tides
local.b: Metrolink will suspend Orange County Line service between Laguna Niguel/Mission Viejo and Oceanside Oct. 26 to 30 amid a coastal flood warning. No buses will replace it.
local.title: Metrolink cancels service to Oceanside next week as south OC braces for high tides

local.h: Inglewood breaks ground on stadium shuttle
local.b: Inglewood broke ground on the $287.5 million Inglewood Transit Connector, which will link the Metro K Line to the city's stadium district. Officials hope it revives the Market Street corridor.

goodnews.h: Pershing Square station renamed for Biddy Mason
goodnews.b: Metro's board voted unanimously to rename the downtown station after Biddy Mason, who went from enslavement to owning much of what is now downtown Los Angeles.
goodnews.title: Metro votes to rename Pershing Square station after pioneering Black Angeleno Biddy Mason

local.h: 5 men charged in 2 Manhattan manhole cases
local.b: Police arrested five men on trespassing and other charges in two separate manhole cases in Upper Manhattan. Two told police they went into the sewer looking for jewelry.
local.title: 5 men charged with trespassing in 2 Manhattan manhole cases

local.h: Mamdani extends ban on new street fairs
local.b: The administration is extending a decades-old moratorium on new street fairs through 2027, citing NYPD overtime. Fairs held this year can still renew.
local.title: Mamdani extends ban on permits for new street fairs due to NYPD overtime

local.h: Countdown clocks coming to NYC bus stops
local.b: The city transportation department struck a deal to bring countdown clocks to more bus stops, so riders across the five boroughs can see how long they'll wait.
local.title: Countdown clocks are coming to an NYC bus stop near you

local.h: EU approves new rights for travellers
local.b: The European Parliament gave final approval to new passenger safeguards, including full refunds for cancelled flights booked through travel agents or online platforms. It passed 652 to 2.
local.title: EU parliament approves more safeguards for travellers in Europe

local.h: Trappes shooting probed as possibly Islamophobic
local.b: A 39-year-old suspect is in custody after shootings in Trappes and La Verrière that killed one person. The interior minister said he fired at a children's playground, a fuel station and a medical centre.
local.title: One person killed in suspected ‘Islamophobic’ shooting near Paris

local.h: France jails 217 in fast-track riot trials
local.b: French courts have jailed 217 people over the rioting, out of about 2,700 detained since Saturday, Justice Minister Gérald Darmanin said.

local.h: Storm Austen cuts power to 161,000 homes
local.b: Storm Austen hit Brittany with gusts up to 140km/h, disrupting trains and closing roads in Brittany and Normandy. Much of northern and central France, including the Paris region, is on alert as it moves east.

local.h: France tightens security before weekend protests
local.b: Macron was due to meet his defence council and security forces Friday as cities limited gatherings and public transport. Only union demonstrations will be authorised this weekend, drawing criticism from student groups.

local.h: DOJ sending election monitors to King County
local.b: The Justice Department says it will send monitors to King County for the Nov. 3 midterms and that they only observe. Washington votes almost entirely by mail.
local.title: DOJ sending election monitors to WA’s King County

goodnews.h: Redmond startup's solar robot pulls weeds
goodnews.b: Aigen's solar-powered robot uses metal arms to pluck weeds as it rolls through farm plots, aiming to weed crops without diesel or herbicide spraying.
goodnews.title: Redmond-based startup develops new robot weeder using AI technology

goodnews.h: Bass drummer hired to drown out street preacher
goodnews.b: A Seattle resident paid a drummer to follow a megaphone-wielding street preacher for over an hour, and the clips went viral on Reddit.
